title: Normalized curve restriction and finite stalk comparison data
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with base $k_0$, algebraic closure $k$ and geometric Frobenius [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega:\operatorname{Type}(u+1)$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $m\ge1$, $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, and $h_0:C_0\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$ a closed immersion with $C_0$ finite type over $k_m$. Use the common-stage constructible Weil heart [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex; def-weil-constructible-heart], classical lisse Weil sheaves and filtrations [def-zl-classical-weil-filtration-transport-data], and normalized classical realization [def-zl-normalized-classical-weil-realization]. Define $f$ as the arithmetic composite of $h_0$ with constant projection and $h$ as its geometric composite through the canonical constant-extension fibre isomorphism [def-dl-a1-constant-extension-data]. For a restriction functor $R$, put $R_C=h_0^*\circ R$, using the actual Weil inverse image [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define the separatedness witnesses by base change and composition. The structure $\mathrm{ZlCurveClassicalPullback}$ consists of a completed-system comparison [def-per-lisse-completed-system-data], classical and geometric inverse-image functors, their forgetful comparison, finite locally free model comparisons, the normalized common-stage underlying and constant comparisons, the ordered Weil equation, the inverse-compositor normalization, and the geometric and Weil realization comparisons with their underlying equation. Define the point-base isomorphism by normalized point sections, the finite stalk isomorphism by pulling back the carrier comparison and using the inverse pullback compositor, then degree-zero cohomology and scalar extension; define finite Frobenius by extending the recorded local operator [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. The structure $\mathrm{ZlCurveFiniteModel}(R,\alpha,H)$ consists of one coefficient field, source and target Weil complexes, isomorphisms realizing them as $H$ and $R_CH$, a finite carrier pullback comparison, and its specified equality after coefficient inclusion. Define $\mathrm{ZlCurveLocalConclusions}$ to mean existence of such a model and, at every closed $z$, closedness of $f(z)$, positive residue degree $d$, $q_z=q_{f(z)}^d$, the reverse-local-factor root multiset formula under $a\mapsto a^d$, and the normalized finite stalk Frobenius intertwining equation for every finite model and compatible residue embeddings [def-wf-iota-real]. Finally define $\mathrm{ZlCurveRestrictionFiltrationSpectrum}$ to assert existence of the normalized classical comparison and pulled-back filtration with its prescribed terms and maps, both heart transports, zero initial term, short exactness, lissity and local conclusions for each term or quotient, and preservation of reality. These are concrete definitions and structures, and assert no existence theorem by themselves. Package the equality comparison between common-stage pullback of a finite inclusion and inclusion of the finite rational pullback as the explicitly constructed isomorphism $\mathrm{zlCurveFiniteInclusionIso}$; the finite-model normalization uses its hom. This is the same literal object-formula equality, with no new choice.
